mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds rate (FEDFUNDS) rises above 5%, it indicates a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to lower S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs increase and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances when FEDFUNDS > 5%, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points within a month signals a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 5-day returns in more than 50% of the instances when UNRATE rises > 0.5pp, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real GDP (GDPC1) by more than 1% quarter-over-quarter signals strengthening economic demand, which is typically associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 60-day returns in more than 30% of the instances when GDPC1 increases > 1% QoQ, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% month-over-month signals supply chain disruptions, which historically lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances when INDPRO decreases > 2% MoM, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) increase by more than 10% month-over-month, it signals a strengthening demand in the housing market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 20-day returns in more than 30% of the instances when HOUST increases > 10% MoM, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 jobs in a month, it signals a strong labor market, which is typically associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of the months when PAYEMS increases by more than 200,000 jobs, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) both rise simultaneously, it indicates inflationary pressure and tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 60-day returns in more than 40% of the instances when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL rise, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP (GDPC1) and retail sales (RSAFS) both increase, it signals robust economic demand, which is typically associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 60-day returns in more than 30% of the instances when both GDPC1 and RSAFS increase, this hypothesis is rejected.
